subject: scorpion
reasoning:
I'm planning a stylized scorpion model, roughly 15-18cm long with a curled tail, and working out the skeleton structure starting from a root body joint before building out the limb chains.

For the limbs, I'm sketching joint hierarchies: a prosoma/head chain, a curling tail chain ending in a stinger, pincer arms with hinged movable fingers, and eight legs using limb IK, all sized to meters with the body resting around 3.5-4cm off the ground.

Now I'm working out the tail's swept geometry — tapering radius with a subtle oscillating bulge along its length, rendered as a six-sided sweep, then capping it with a venom sac sphere and a spike-shaped stinger oriented along the tail's end tangent.

For the body I'm building the mesosoma as a series of tapering box "plates" strung along the body bone, giving it a blocky, puppet-like segmented look, with a dark amber shell color and contrasting plate and edge tones.

Still building the head and jaw structure...

Now I'm sketching out the pedipalp arm chains with shoulder, elbow, and wrist joints extending forward and outward for the pincer gesture.

Placing fine-grained arm joint coordinates...

Still placing joints and chains...

Still defining leg joints...

Continuing the tail curve with points through T7, keeping total height around 0.19, and checking foot and abdomen clearances so the lowest points sit just above the floor plane.

For the tail I'm placing small dorsal spikes along the sweep using an along-path helper, orienting each spike outward at the dorsal normal, then adding the venom sac as a small scaled sphere near the tail's tip before working out the stinger itself.

For the stinger, I'm computing it as a spike using the tail end's position and tangent direction, bonded to the last tail joint so it inherits motion, with a small base offset so it buries into the sac. For the carapace I'm applying a mottled paint texture using two shell colors, and for the pincers I'm considering adding tiny stud-like spikes on the palm for granulation detail.

Now I'm placing eye positions and sizes relative to the carapace box dimensions: median eyes as small black spheres near the top center, lateral eyes as smaller spheres at the front corners, and I'm working out the spacing for seven dorsal plates running along the body's z-axis.

I'm computing each plate's position, width, and height so they narrow and shorten toward the tail, plus a flatter sternite underneath and alternating shading between plates for visual variety.

Now I'm setting up the tail radius taper with a periodic bulge, then defining the jaw joint and chelicerae as paired boxes on the head and jaw bones, with upper and lower segments positioned symmetrically on either side.

Setting up arm chains and claw joints...
